subject: OrbitHealth — Pricing & invoice estimate
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@orbithealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: OrbitHealth — Pricing & invoice estimate

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery:

What we heard
- Production use case: real-time clinical summarization and triage for inbound patient messages (web + mobile).
- Typical prompt size: 300–700 tokens per request; peak multistep flows up to ~1,200 tokens.
- Expected steady-state volume: 15M–25M tokens / month (with burst up to ~40M).
- Important constraints: HIPAA controls, VPC private deployment is preferred but trialing hosted first is ok.

Cost/qualification items (requested on call)
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of ~$750 / 1M tokens for gen workloads (post-aggregation).
- Need split: inference gen tokens vs embeddings for search / semantic similarity.
- Contract preference: 12-month committed capacity with quarterly reviews.

What I attached
- OrbitHealth_pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx — per-model unit costs, batching assumptions, projected monthly token consumption scenarios (Low / Base / High).
- invoice_estimate_OH-2026-0912.pdf — a simple invoice-format estimate showing monthly and annual totals under the Base scenario.

Top-level pricing note (provisional)
- Baseline hosted gen rate (recommended model family): $0.92 / 1K input+output tokens (equates to $920 / 1M tokens).
- With model selection and 15–25M tokens/mo volume + 10% committed-discount and batching/KV caching assumptions, we can get close to your $750 / 1M tokens target (approx $760–$810 / 1M depending on seq length profile).
- Embeddings: $0.20 / 1K tokens (rough placeholder) — will refine once you provide % of traffic that is embeddings vs gen.

Next steps
1) Could you confirm a monthly budget range and the expected % of traffic that will be embeddings vs generation? (e.g., 80% gen / 20% embeddings)
2) We can run a short costing experiment on a 7-day sample of logs (if you can share a sanitized sample) to pin the sequence length distribution.
3) I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the spreadsheet and agree on a committed capacity cadence.

Available times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT. If those don’t work I’ll send a calendar link.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

-----

Attachment: invoice_estimate_OH-2026-0912.pdf (PDF)

Date: 2026-11-09T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OrbitHealth — Pricing & invoice estimate

Sean —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifications before the follow-up:

- Budget: we’re looking at an initial committed budget band of $60k–$120k / month for inference (hosted + reserved for production later). We need the invoice to show both committed and on-demand scenarios.
- Embeddings vs gen split: rough estimate today is 70% gen, 30% embeddings. Gen average ~550 tokens/request.
- Can you confirm which model variant you used for the estimate (Redwood-curated 13B q4 / or wider family)? If you have a low-latency variant that materially reduces cost per 1M tokens, please flag it.

Also please confirm expected SLOs for P99 latency under the Base scenario — our clinical flows have a 500ms target for single-turn summarization.

If you can update the spreadsheet with the committed vs on-demand rows and call out the model used, we’ll review and confirm a time to sync.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Product — Clinical Platforms
Orbit Health
jordan.lee@orbithealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0246

Subject: Re: OrbitHealth — Pricing & invoice estimate

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick note and the budget band — helpful. I updated the attached spreadsheet and regenerated the invoice PDF to show both the Committed (12-month) and On-Demand rows under the Base token scenario. Summary of changes: 

- Model used: Redwood-curated 13B quantized variant (q4_1) for Base; we included an alternative low-latency 7B family variant in tab "AltModels" that lowers projected cost to ~$650 / 1M tokens but increases risk on hallucination-sensitive tasks (we call this out in the notes).
- Committed pricing: assumes a 12-month commit at 20M tokens/month baseline with quarterly reconciliation. That gets to ~$730 / 1M tokens effective across the year (depending on actual token mix).
- On-demand: listed at the baseline hosted rate (no commit), ~$920 / 1M tokens as shown in the earlier email.
- P99 latency: estimated 350–450ms for single-turn summarization on the q4_1 13B variant under our Dedicated SLO profile; hosted may be slightly higher ~450–600ms depending on concurrency — we can scope Dedicated pools if you need consistent 500ms P99.

Attachments: updated OrbitHealth_pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx and invoice_estimate_OH-2026-0912.pdf (both attached). Also added a Drive link with the costing workbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfPricingCalc

Proposed next step: 30-min review on Tue 11/12 at 10:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite. If you prefer me to include one of our infra engineers (Laura) for the latency/capacity discussion, I’ve cc’d her.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
